analysis.subject: finance
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers age appropriate conversations about teen saving, building emergency funds, choosing safe places to save, workplace retirement options, and an early investing example showing how compound interest grows savings over time.

overview.headline: Saving habits for teens: emergency funds and early compound growth

keyPoints.point: Help teens set up a savings program where at least 10 percent of earnings goes directly into savings account
keyPoints.quote: Once your teen has a steady job, help them set up a savings program so that at least 10 percent of earnings goes directly into their savings account.

keyPoints.point: Keep at least three months worth of living expenses saved for emergency needs to avoid high interest credit options
keyPoints.quote: “A good rule to live by is to save 10 percent of what you earn, and have at least three months’ worth of living expenses saved up in case of an emergency.”

keyPoints.point: Compound interest means earning interest on both saved money and previously earned interest to accelerate growth
keyPoints.quote: Compound interest is when your child earns interest on both the money they save and the interest they earn.

keyPoints.point: Setting aside $100 every year starting at age 14 at 5 percent every year can grow to about $23,000 by age 65 compared to about $7,000 starting at age 35
keyPoints.quote: Show your child the following: If they set aside $100 every year starting at age 14, they'd have about $23,000 at age 65.

keyTerms.gloss: money set aside to cover living expenses when an emergency occurs without using credit
keyTerms.quote: Explain to your child that they sometimes may need to choose between adding money to a 401(k) or to their emergency savings.

keyTerms.gloss: interest earned on both saved money and previously earned interest
keyTerms.quote: Compound interest is when your child earns interest on both the money they save and the interest they earn.

keyTerms.gloss: percentage charged or paid for using money, relevant when choosing a savings account
keyTerms.quote: When choosing to open a savings account at a bank or credit union, explain that the interest rate may not be as relevant since the goal is to save enough money to cover emergency expenses.

keyTerms.gloss: workplace retirement account where employers may provide matching contributions as an incentive to save
keyTerms.quote: Explain to your child that once they start a job, they may be offered a retirement account at work called a 401(k).

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Checks core definitions and rules before teens calculate tradeoffs between emergency savings and retirement options
componentPlan.focusQuote: Compound interest is when your child earns interest on both the money they save and the interest they earn.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Contrasting early versus later start makes the cost of waiting visible side by side without merging recurring and lump sums
